purpose: TASK-029 Goods Receipt Draft create, update and cancel over real HTTP, JWT and MySQL: receivable-PO gate, full replace across UOM, warehouse, bin and status, typed refusals for foreign lines, wrong UOM, bin outside its warehouse, duplicate buckets, zero quantity and stale versions, the Inventory-bound reason byte rule, cancel only in DRAFT, permission, replay and the duplicate delivery-note warning; PO progress and Inventory unchanged. Carries the unchanged TASK-025 and TASK-028 cases; Opening parser, precheck and scoped atomic posting guard against invalid/double stock writes, stale Item codes and unsafe lot keys. TASK-032 adds HTTP/JWT/MySQL confirmation against real Inventory posting: atomic two-line posting, PO progress/history, procurement audit and full receipt, idempotent replay and event conflict, locked over-receipt and reasons, inactive or mismatched locations, rollback after posting or subsequent write failures, blocked supplier quarantine, invalid/empty lines and missing lot, permission/version/state refusals, SKU tracking drift and short-expiry authorization and evidence. Three TASK-033 real HTTP/MySQL cases verify operation owner and permission loss, receipt list/detail, and receivable PO/warehouse/bin lookups. TASK-037 adds a read-only outstanding PO route, checking delivery-date precedence, scope, paging, invalid filters and HTTP 401/403. Date bounds require outstanding quantity on a line whose delivery date is within range, using the PO header delivery date only when the line's delivery date is absent. G3 checks version-bound one-way Opening close, strong authentication, durable replay, rollback with a failed success audit and visibility/disabled writes on LIVE and stale reconciliation. The Inventory report cases verify shared stock and movement filters, a stable maximum projection and rejection without partial output or data after a permission change or abort. G5 extends the global configuration normalization assertion to include the company section. The pinned company module reads environment variables; workload scale and case count are unchanged. P1 adds two exact cases for receipt source list filtering and purchase currency, and for confirmed source snapshots, current lock ownership and whole-batch rejection on ineligible, mixed-supplier or mixed-currency inputs.
data: TASK-029 file: 9 registrations sharing one application and pool; 2 users, 1 supplier, 1 item, 2 UOMs, 2 SKUs, 3 SKU-UOMs, 2 warehouses, 3 bins; at most 3 POs, 2 GRs and 4 details per case, POs written by SQL; about 50 HTTP requests in the file, with the per-IP request limit raised for the test application only. TASK-025 and TASK-028 data unchanged. No fixture files; Opening routine adds 7 in-memory cases with at most 5,001 small lines in a parser-only count check, otherwise at most 6 lines. Explicit local Opening suite: original 9 plus 5 new G3 cases, 14 total, one fresh isolated MySQL 26.7 schema, one warehouse, two bins, two SKUs and two actors, at most two positive rows per file. TASK-032: 9 registrations share one application and pool, with 3 users and 3 roles, 1 supplier, 1 item, 2 UOMs, 2 SKUs, 3 SKU-UOM links, 2 warehouses and 3 bins. The file creates 9 two-line POs by SQL, 10 GR drafts by HTTP and issues 30 serial confirm requests. Per case: 1 PO, at most 2 GRs and 6 confirm requests; per request: at most 2 lines and 2 details. In-process fault stubs are restored in finally. C5 uses one short-lived DB_ADMIN fixture connection only to create and drop the same temporary PO progress trigger, with drop in finally and connection close after the case. All HTTP application SQL still runs under the original application account; the per-IP request limit applies to the test application only. All TASK-032 fixtures are inline. Extends the shared Confirm fixture with one receiving user/role and one temporary lapsed-permission user/role in C8. Adds five two-line POs, three drafts, three confirms and 19 sequential GET requests across three cases. A bin is made inactive and restored. No additional runner or fixture files. One new functional HTTP/MySQL registration reuses the existing two-user fixture and makes four single-line POs (confirmed, partially received, closed, cancelled), four create requests and eleven serial outstanding GET requests. G3 separately adds three in-memory page cases proposed for routine client CI. Author and TL Playwright use a private synthetic schema and are local evidence only, outside this receipt. Inventory quantity reports add four in-memory functional server cases using the existing mocked inquiry executor. The 5,001 null placeholders exercise a rejection branch, with no physical query execution or data generation. The separate real browser case uses two synthetic opening rows and remains local only. P1 list case creates one PO and one GR draft and adds one actor without purchasing permission. The source case creates four POs and five GRs (four confirmations, at most eight details), one opposing supplier and a second currency. A 21-ID request is an in-memory invalid input and writes no rows.
concurrency: Within a case: 1, with no concurrent requests. Runner workers unchanged; Opening cases serial per file, one isolated database and HTTP app for the explicit local cases only. G3 cases run serially in the existing explicit local script; no additional application worker, DB pool, or browser CI job. The four added assertions add no database connections, parallel requests or runner workers. The P1 source case holds one read transaction and tests one competing NOWAIT transaction at a time. Worker and runner settings are unchanged.
repetitions: 1 per applicable existing run. The four report tests run once through existing functional discovery.
thresholds: All cases pass; coverage floors unchanged; no timing threshold; Opening requires 7 inherited routine unit cases plus 3 new G3 page cases, and 14/14 explicit local cases (original 9 plus new G3 5), all zero skips. All 9 TASK-032 cases must pass, including exact stock and PO effects, zero additional effect on replay or rejection, atomic rollback of injected faults, and persisted exception evidence. All three new cases and all inherited cases must pass, with existing coverage floors. All four added report cases pass, and all existing coverage and functional thresholds remain.
trigger: The existing ci.yml triggers in the existing server jobs; no new job. The existing discovery covers the Opening routine units and would cover the 3 G3 page cases after approval. The 14 guarded native cases (original 9 plus G3 5) run only via explicit local server/scripts/inventoryOpening.integration.js. No CI job, discovery flag or workflow change. TASK-032 uses the existing server integration discovery and job. Existing functional CI unit discovery for the four report cases. No new job, capacity case, scenario repetition or Playwright CI extent. The two P1 registrations each run once in the existing functional server integration discovery.
cost: Not measured. A 2026-11-19 local serial run of the 12 Purchasing integration files (107 cases) was history, not a promise. No capacity workload; Seven small Opening units with no database calls, no separate CI overhead measurement. Historical original 9/9 explicit local MySQL/HTTP suite took about 1.3 seconds after schema migration. No new non-functional workload. TASK-032 CI execution time has not been measured. This adds a serial functional suite without a timing or capacity workload. The TASK-037 HTTP registration is covered by the local isolated MySQL regression; CI duration is unmeasured. The single new HTTP case ran in 0.73 seconds locally. G3 complete 14-case local MySQL/HTTP suite measured 2.60 s after migrations. Author client regression (47 cases including the three additions) ran in about 1.3 s locally. CI overhead not measured; no new job/capacity. The focused 23-case server file ran in 0.128 s locally including the original cases and startup. Incremental hosted CI time has not been measured. No new runner or capacity spending. P1 ran 40 affected MySQL cases per timezone in a disposable schema and rehearsed one existing Chromium flow per timezone outside CI. The incremental CI cost is unmeasured.
